subject: Reserved capacity tenor trigger and discount flow for QuantLeap
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@quantleap.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@quantleap.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sizing ask + pricing mechanics for reserved pool

Jordan — thanks again for the demo last week. QuantLeap is ready to move from pilot to production but we need clarity on two things before we sign:

1) Sizing: we expect 600 concurrent user sessions at peak (30M tokens/mo), generating mostly short chat and embeddings traffic. We'd like a recommended reserved GPU footprint (A100/H100 equivalence) and the risk buffer you typically recommend.

2) Pricing sensitivity: our CFO is nervous about fixed 24-month commits given volatile GPU market pricing. We're open to a 12 mo anchor but want a mechanism that caps our exposure if GPU spot/index moves +20% up or down. Is Redwood open to a dual-tenor + index-trigger that reduces discount or provides credits when GPU market swings?

Can you send a worksheet/term example we can share with finance?

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Product
QuantLeap

[Attachment: QuantLeap_initial_traffic_estimates.csv (csv)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@quantleap.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask + pricing mechanics for reserved pool

Sara — appreciate the clear ask. High level answers up front, workbook attached.

Sizing recommendation (quick):
- Baseline: 3 x H100 equivalence for steady throughput (model mix: chat + embeddings).
- Burst/peak buffer: +30% (to cover concurrent session spikes) => reserve equivalent of 4 GPUs.
- Autoscaling for short bursts remains enabled on Dedicated; reserved pool covers steady-state and predictable peaks.

Pricing mechanism options we typically offer (we can tailor):
A) Fixed 12-month with smaller discount, 24-month with larger discount (standard).
B) Indexed collar (your idea): a mild indexation clause tied to a GPU index (monthly) with a ceiling/floor. Example: discount steps down by up to 6% if index rises >15% and credits applied if index falls >15%.
C) Safety-credit approach: 12-month commit + defined credits equal to X% of monthly invoice if our internal GPU cost delta exceeds a cap — helpful for procurement since it avoids re-pricing mid-contract.

I've looped in Karthik (who owns pricing policy) and Evelyn (who handles capacity planning) — Marcus from finance will review the dollar math. See attached \"QuantLeap_Sizing_Workbook.xlsx\" and draft SOW.

Next step: can we get procurement's preferred tenor/thresholds so Karthik can model a formal term sheet?

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: QuantLeap_Sizing_Workbook.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 14:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask + pricing mechanics for reserved pool

Team — ran three scenarios in the workbook: 12m, 18m, 24m tenor. Key observations:

1) Discount table (list-price baseline):
- 12m: 18% discount (conservative)
- 18m: 24% discount (mid)
- 24m: 30% discount (commit favored)

2) Exposure to GPU price swings: with a strict fixed-price 24m we take most of the upside/downside risk. To make this acceptable to Redwood finance we need either an index collar or a graduated discount clawback tied to a transparent hardware cost index. I've modeled an index-collar (floor -10% / ceiling +20%) where above +20% we apply a partial surcharge (max +6%) and below -10% we issue service credits (max 5% monthly).

3) Sizing margin & sku mix: Evelyn's capacity plan shows reserving 4 H100-equivalent instances with room to move 20% headroom between Reserved and Burst capacity. That buys QuantLeap predictable latency at p99 while keeping our cluster utilization leverage.

Requesting approvals: Marcus — can finance greenlight the collar parameters (max surcharge +6%, credit cap 5%) for enterprise deals up to $1.2M ARR? If not, what's the alternative guardrail (e.g., shorter tenor or lower discount)?

Karthik
Director, Commercial Strategy

[Inline: summary of model outputs attached to the workbook]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 16:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask + pricing mechanics for reserved pool

Karthik — reviewed the scenarios. Quick decision path:

- Approve index-collar pilot for Strategic mid-market deals (<= $1.5M ARR) with parameters: floor -12% credits up to 6%, ceiling +22% surcharge capped at +6%. Pilot limited to 6 accounts and requires monthly reporting to Finance and Product Ops.
- Require sales to price 18m as default for collar deals (balance between risk & retention). 24m stays available but requires Finance Exec sign-off.
- Sizing guardrail: reserve 4 H100-equivalent for QuantLeap with documented conversion to A100-equivalents in the SOW (to maintain flexibility across infra).

Jordan — you have finance approval to propose the collar pilot to QuantLeap under a 18-month anchor with the above caps. Send me the final term sheet for signature and loop Legal for a short addendum to the MSA.

Marcus Lin
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: QL_reserved_commit_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)]
